bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM: 3.5 lakh students to get live JEE-NEET preparation through model schools
bihar_raw_news.content: Government Policies 2 min read Bihar CM: 3.5 lakh students to get live JEE-NEET preparation through model schools The Chief Minister further highlighted the development in the education sector, stating that the State government has established 700 model schools, with a capacity of 3.5 lakh students to provide top-notch online education through live classes, similar to Kota, Rajasthan. ANI Published On Sep 23, 2026 at 10:11 AM IST Select ETEducation as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary outlines major push for education, energy sectors Patna: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday outlined his government's focus on the energy and education sectors in the State, detailing major advancements in digital education and electricity for the general public. Addressing the gathering at the 'Bihar Ke Sachche Nayak - Real Heroes of Bihar' program, the Chief Minister revealed that 1.7 crore families have not received an electricity bill for an entire year, while only 22 lakh families currently pay for their power. "There are 1 crore 70 lakh families who have not received an electricity bill for a year. 1 crore 70 lakh. There are only 22 lakh families who receive electricity bills, friends. We said that this should also be connected to solar power because we need to move out of subsidies as well," he said. Advt He emphasised that the State allocates approximately Rs 6,000 crore for agricultural feeders in rural areas, adding that Bihar will prosper when Biharis become strong. "We provide agricultural feeders in villages. We give about 6,000 crore rupees for agricultural feeders. That is why there are many things that need to be organised. Bihar's prosperity will only happen when we Biharis become strong. And Biharis stand on their own resources," he said. The Chief Minister further highlighted the development in the education sector, stating that the State government has established 700 model schools , with a capacity of 3.5 lakh students to provide top-notch online education through live classes, similar to Kota, Rajasthan. "We have established 700 model schools. 3.5 lakh children study in these 700 model schools. We started organising facilities for these 3.5 lakh children; along with online education, we started live classes," he said. "We saw that in Kota, lakhs of our children go to prepare for JEE and NEET. We said that we will provide preparation for JEE and NEET to 3.5 lakh children right on the land of Bihar. We did this in model schools," he added. In addition, Choudhary highlighted the impact of the 'Vidyarthi Sathi App', designed to support late-night studying, stating that over 1,42,000 students are actively learning online through the app as late as 1:00 AM. Advt "I made an arrangement through the Vidyarthi Sathi App. Now, teachers are available to them on it. And you will be pleased to know that 1,42,000 children are studying online at 1:00 AM at night," he said. (ANI) ANI Published

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Long leave by chiefs of 3 police organisations raise eyebrows
bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar bureaucracy is grappling with the reality of chiefs of three important police organisations proceeding on long leaves. Bihar DGP Vinay Kumar is on a 21-day leave, while Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) Chairperson Parmar Ravi Manubhai is away for 25 days and Bihar Police Subordinate Services Commission (BPSSC) Chairperson K S Dwivedi has proceeded on a month-long leave. Further, the Government has made alternative arrangements for two of the organisations. Preeta Verma takes additional charge as acting DGP, while Harjot Kaur Bamhra assumes additional responsibility as BPSC Chairman. But no interim arrangement has yet been announced for BPSSC. Absence of chiefs of three important police institutions in Bihar’s administrative and police framework has raised many eyebrows. national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Regional News 59 Ministry of Ayush to host 11th Ayurveda Day in Nagpur with focus on healthier
national_raw_news.content: The inaugural ceremony of 11th Ayurveda Day, based on the theme “ Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow,” will be held at the Kavivarya Suresh Bhat Auditorium in Nagpur from 9 to 10 AM this morning. Vice-Chancellor of the National Institute of Ayurveda, Jaipur, Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, informing about this event, said that this year’s Ayurveda Day will focus on strengthening Ayurveda through evidence, research and innovation, while promoting community health and well-being. Director of the Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences, Delhi, Dr. Shiv Kumar Sarin, will address a scientific session on “Integrating Therapies is needed to reduce NCD (Non-Communicable Diseases) Burden by 2027”. Subsequently, Dr. Geeta Krishnan Pillai, Unit Head of the Global Traditional Medicine Centre, Jamnagar, will speak on “Shashwatam to Vishwas – Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow and the Road to 2047” The programme will also witness the launch of “From Traditional Wisdom to Global Leadership: Ayush Vision 2030” Report, the Status Report on Ayush-related Inventions in India, and the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences – Ayurveda Gyan Naipunya Initiative)CCRAS-AGNI an Assessment Scale Web Portal. Ayurveda institutions, practitioners and various stakeholders from across the country and the world will participate in the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations. Dhananjay Wankhede, Akashvani News, Nagpur.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Games: Indian rower Balraj Panwar qualifies for Men’s Singles sculls finals 1 hour ago 33
national_raw_news.content: At the Asian Games, India is looking to build on its medal tally on Day Four today at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan, with several athletes and teams competing across disciplines. Indian swimmer Beniston Benedicton has qualified for the final of the men’s 100-metre butterfly event. He finished ninth overall in the heats to secure his place in the final which will be held at 1:38 PM today. In rowing at the Asian Games, Balraj Panwar has qualified for the final of the men’s singles sculls event. He finished third in his heat with a timing of 6 minutes 52.84 seconds and was fourth overall across the two heats. The final will be held tomorrow. India have also secured final berth in the men’s double sculls event. Satnam Singh and Salman Khan finished second in their heat, clocking 6 minutes 15.63 seconds. They finished fourth overall across the two heats and advanced to the final. In Sepaktakraw, Indian Men’s Regu team defeated Philippines, 2-nil in the opening Group B match, registering 15-7, 15-10 win. Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu will take part in the women’s 49-kilogram final. The match is scheduled to begin at 10 AM. She will be aiming for her first Asian Games medal after finishing fourth at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. In shooting, Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker alongside Suruchi Singh and Esha Singh are competing in the team event and individual qualification in the women’s 10-metre air pistol event. India is already assured of medals in Men’s badminton and Women’s Wushu. The Men’s badminton team will take on China in the semi-final today, after defeating Japan in the quarter-final yesterday. Tha match is schduled to begin at 11:30 AM. In Wushu, Roshibina Devi will face Indonesia’s Thania Kusumaningtyas in the women’s 60-kilogram Sanda semi-final at 2:50 PM. India’s skeet shooters Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan will be in action on the final day of qualification, while the women’s skeet team will also compete. In Hockey,the Indian Women’s Team will face Thailand in their third Pool B match this morning. The match will begin 11:30 AM. Indian Men’s and Women’s kabaddi teams will also continue their group-stage campaigns. Indian athletes will also compete in canoe sprint, fencing, squash, swimming, table tennis, boxing, equestrian and soft tennis. Yesterday, the Indian women’s cricket team clinched country’s first gold medal of the Games, defeating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final. The victory took India’s medal tally to seven. In Boxing, Jadumani Singh advanced to the pre-quarterfinals in the Men’s 55-kilogram category, while Sakshi Chaudhary also progressed to the pre-quarterfinals.
